newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call trades in narrow range on good supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian call trades in narrow range on good supply.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday in the 5.50-5.75 percent range in dull trade, unchanged from the day's opening levels, dealers said.
"It was another dull day," a dealer at a foreign bank said.
"Trade was in a narrow range throughout the day."
Dealers said yields on government securities were largely steady on Friday.
"There was little movement in prices," a dealer said. "There is some demand for short-dated securities but buyers and sellers are not able to match prices."
Securities with a one-year maturity traded at a yield of 13.01 percent against 13.04 percent on Thursday, dealers said.
The 13.50 percent 1998 stock was traded at 13.46 percent against 13.49 percent while there was no change in the 13.62 percent 1998 stock at 13.52 percent.

Dealers said three-month certificates of deposit were quoted around 11 percent. Three-month commercial paper rates were between 13.50-15.50 percent, depending on the credit rating of the corporate, a dealer at a foreign bank said.
Rates on intercorporate deposits remained steady in the 17.0-19.0 percent range for top-rated borrowers.
